name: ssh
plain: `ssh` opens a secure, encrypted session on another computer, runs one command there, or builds an encrypted tunnel for other traffic. It is how you log into OverTheWire, Linux servers and lab VMs.
Besides logging in, ssh can forward ports (reach a service that is hidden behind a firewall) and run as a SOCKS proxy for your browser or scanner.
when: Log into OverTheWire games and lab machines.
Run a command on a remote host without opening a shell.
Forward a port (-L, -R) or build a proxy (-D) to reach internal services.

mistakes: Keys with the wrong permissions are refused: chmod 600 for private keys.
Host key changed warnings: do not just delete the entry; first confirm the host really changed.
Forgetting -N with -L: you get a shell as well as the tunnel.
Using -A to a host you do not control: they can use your agent while you are connected.
Passing the port with a capital P (that is scp); ssh uses lowercase -p.
try: Set up -L to reach a local python3 -m http.server through ssh to localhost.
Use -J to reach a second VM through the first.
Write a ~/.ssh/config entry for an OverTheWire game and check it with ssh -G.
Build a SOCKS proxy with -D and fetch a page with curl --socks5-hostname.
